hypothesis: The same broad channel must drive both overshoot and trough in every episode.
evidence: 2014 trough is operating-cost driven even though initial overshoot is FX/valuation.
interpretation: Broad-channel identity fails at least in 2014.

hypothesis: Every episode should rotate to a totally different broad channel during drawdown.
evidence: 2018 and 2023 drawdowns are largely reversals of the same broad valuation/margin family.
interpretation: Reversal within a channel family is as important as channel substitution.

hypothesis: Late credit deterioration should dominate the profitability trough.
evidence: 2014 Apr incobrability charges stable; 2018 Nov margin drop is explained mainly by lower securities/FX; 2023 Q3-24 drawdown predates material household mora.
interpretation: Credit losses are late/secondary in the identified trough months.

hypothesis: An overshoot from devaluation/financial margin implies a persistent pro-bank effect.
evidence: 2014 Jan overshoot collapses by Feb; 2018 May gains later face funding/margin reversal; 2023 Q4 ROA 12.1 falls to 1.9 3m by Sep-24.
interpretation: Initial valuation gains can be transitory.

hypothesis: Large positive titles/FX/CER components identify the full benefit.
evidence: 2023 simultaneously has large interest expense and monetary losses; 2014/2018 also have operating/funding/credit offsets.
interpretation: Keep gross channel contributions separate from ROA/net profit.

hypothesis: All episodes can be compared at identical frequency and accounting basis.
evidence: 2014/2018 use monthly nominal accounting; 2023/24 uses homogeneous-currency quarterly/3m views.
interpretation: Compare channel direction and phase, not numeric magnitudes across vintages.
